observations: Fiscal year basis: all BHP values are for financial years ending 30 June (FY2023 = 1 Jul 2022 - 30 Jun 2023); year field = FY end year.

Site-level (operated asset) water data is only provided for FY2023; FY2019-FY2023 is corporate-only. Data excludes OZ Minerals (acquired FY2023) and discontinued operations (BHP Mitsui Coal, Petroleum). Values rounded to nearest 10 ML.

Water-stress classification change: withdrawals in water stress areas were 233,190 ML (FY2021) and 246,700 ML (FY2022) but only 29,710 ML in FY2023 (Environment!E19:G19). In FY2023 only Legacy assets and Pampa Norte are flagged as in water stress (Water!E7, I7); Escondida (226,190 ML, largely seawater) is no longer flagged, so the drop is a classification/scope change, not a real reduction. Same pattern for discharge (123,200 -> 2,630 ML) and consumption (115,400 -> 33,710 ML) in stress areas.

Methodology change (footnotes Environment!A60 / Water!A119): FY2019-FY2021 withdrawals include only rainfall/run-off captured AND used in-year; from FY2022 (updated ICMM guidance) captured-but-not-used rainfall/run-off is also included. FY2022+ withdrawals and surface-water withdrawals are therefore not comparable with earlier years (surface water jumps 28,710 -> 68,060 ML FY2021->FY2022; Type 2 withdrawals 35,430 -> 67,120 ML).
Other managed water was reported as "diversions" before FY2022; from FY2022 it is broken down by quality type (Environment!A62).

Restatement flag: the Environment and Water sheets state that italic data has been restated since the ESG Standards and Databook 2022. Essentially all FY2019-FY2022 cells on the Environment sheet (and the prior-year rows of the Water 5-year tables) are italic-formatted, so the file does not allow isolating which specific values were restated; records carry a note where the cell is italic.

Nickel West Kwinana withdrawal-by-source was restated for FY2017-FY2019 using site-specific Water Corporation source proportions; from FY2021 all Kwinana supply is reported as third-party (Water!A121). Third-party withdrawals are blank ("-") for FY2019-FY2020 in both the Environment sheet and the Water sheet (H48:H49).

Water quality typing: BHP uses Type 1/2/3 (MCA Water Accounting Framework). Per schema, Type 1 is mapped to withdrawal_fresh; Type 2 and Type 3 are kept as other:withdrawal_type2/type3 (no single stated low-quality total). Note Water!C44 labels Type 2 "High Quality", so under ICMM 2021 conventions high-quality = Type 1 + Type 2.

BMA recycled/reused uses a non-ICMM method (volume returned from operational tasks to water stores) due to climatic variation (Water!A116). Corporate recycled/reused jumped from 260,900 ML (FY2022) to 344,710 ML (FY2023); Pampa Norte alone reports 262,750 ML reused in FY2023 (Water!I31), ~9x its 28,640 ML withdrawal.

Escondida dominates: 226,190 of 408,540 ML FY2023 withdrawals (55%), 213,920 ML of it seawater (desalination) and zero Type 1 water; 121,630 ML discharged to sea. Nickel West consumption (16,870 ML) exceeds withdrawal (16,160 ML), with 16,160 ML "consumption - other".
Consumption FY2020 is stated as 251,969.8 ML (Environment!D29), the only unrounded value in the series. Some cells are text with embedded spaces ("43, 450" in Environment!D15) - parsed as 43,450.

Production is only available as copper-equivalent production (kt Cu-eq) per asset for FY2020-FY2023 in the GHG emissions by asset sheet (recorded as other_production in t Cu-eq); no ore processed or metal production figures in this databook.

FY2023 significant environmental fines: 5 in Australia (all BMA, US$47,503; effluent, tailings and mine-affected-water releases) and 3 in Chile (Escondida, US$6,779; Laguna Seca ponds, groundwater extraction monitoring, air quality). Accidental discharges of water and tailings reported as 0 ML every year FY2019-FY2023 (excludes Samarco dam failure).

Targets: BHP committed to publish context-based water targets (CBWTs) in FY2023, applicable to FY2030, with progress reporting from FY2024 (Social value scorecard!A19/B19). No numeric water target is given in this file.

Water stress is defined via WWF Water Risk Filter (high/very high physical risk) per CEO Water Mandate; SASB EM-MM-140a.1 (WRI Aqueduct basis) is only cross-referenced to bhp.com, not reported in the file.

Duplicated tables (Water!B vs Environment!G, Water 5-year tables rows 45-58, "Water data by asset" sheet) were cross-checked and not recorded twice; they agree except: BHP discharge table Water!B54: Water!B54="–" vs Environment!G21=0 | BHP discharge table Water!B55: Water!B55="–" vs Environment!F21=0 | BHP discharge table Water!B56: Water!B56="–" vs Environment!E21=0 | BHP discharge table Water!B57: Water!B57="–" vs Environment!D21=0 | BHP discharge table Water!B58: Water!B58="–" vs Environment!C21=0 (Type 1 discharge shown as a dash vs 0).
